newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to open won/yen market from October.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to open won/yen market from October.

text.p: South Korea's Finance and Economic Ministry said on Monday it would open a won/yen foreign exchange market from October 1 to modernise the domestic market and to internationalise the local currency.

A ministry statement said won/yen's mid-rate would be set based on the previous day's average exchange rate of the won/dollar and the yen/dollar rate at 8:40 a.m. (2340 GMT) on the Tokyo foreign exchange market.
It said there would be no daily fluctuation limit for the won/yen. Currently, the government limits the won/dollar rate within 2.25 percent on either side of the mid-rate.
The statement said the won/yen trading would be done through the Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute.
Trading will include three spots, such as value-today and value-tomorrow, and 17 forward transactions such as one-to-six days, one week, one month and one year.
The base trading unit will be 10 million yen.
